reading_paths.meaning: Follow a business or family shock into the owner's protection choice, then ask what happens to business investment and household room.
reading_paths.limit: The current sources do not follow the same owner through the choice and later jobs, services or family wealth.

reading_paths.title: When a raise changes the help a family can keep
reading_paths.meaning: Follow an earnings change into the public help that falls away, then ask whether the household has more room and more stable work afterward.
reading_paths.limit: The current sources do not follow the same family through total resources, care costs and work after the change.

reading_paths.title: When the due date is part of the energy burden
reading_paths.meaning: Follow the gap between income and the utility due date into arrears or shutoff, then ask what payment, credit or health cost follows.
reading_paths.limit: The current sources do not establish the full later chain for every household.

reading_paths.title: When health coverage keeps a job in place
reading_paths.meaning: Follow employer coverage into the cost of changing jobs, then ask whether the worker gains or gives up pay, fit and family care access.
reading_paths.limit: The current sources do not compare the full job and coverage choice for the same worker.

reading_paths.title: When debt relief fixes the record but not the illness
reading_paths.meaning: Follow a medical bill into the credit record, then ask whether relief changes the household's later room even when the health need remains.
reading_paths.limit: The current experiment does not connect the credit result to every later housing, work or care choice.

reading_paths.title: When cash changes the shape of a household
reading_paths.meaning: Follow regular cash into rent or mortgage arrears and who lives together, then ask whether the added room lasts after the payment ends.
reading_paths.limit: The current sources do not show that a smaller or changed household is safer or better for every family.

reading_paths.title: When a benefit loss changes the public mood
reading_paths.meaning: Follow a household benefit from cash loss into consumer sentiment, then ask whether trust, blame or voting changes later.
reading_paths.limit: The current study measures sentiment and does not establish the later political step.

reading_paths.title: When the same yearly income buys less certainty
reading_paths.meaning: Follow a change in pay risk into spending and credit, then ask whether the household can still plan, borrow and keep its choices open.
reading_paths.limit: The current sources do not follow the same worker through pay risk, cash reserves and later household outcomes.

reading_paths.title: When a temporary payment becomes a monthly bill
reading_paths.meaning: Follow a one-time payment into a vehicle or other durable purchase, then ask whether financing protects access or narrows later room.
reading_paths.limit: The current sources do not show the same household's need, loan terms and later repayment outcome.

reading_paths.title: When cash changes the rest of the household
reading_paths.meaning: Follow a payment to one person into another member's training, care or spending, then ask what the family gains and what need becomes visible.
reading_paths.limit: The current experiment does not settle the health meaning or the lasting effect after payments end.

reading_paths.title: When new residents change the local customer base
reading_paths.meaning: Follow migration into customer demand, jobs and services, then ask how housing and the value of the place adjust.
reading_paths.limit: The current sources do not show the same place's present housing, wages, public capacity and belonging together.

reading_paths.title: When the first price is not the final price
reading_paths.meaning: Follow a headline price into the fee shown later, then ask whether the household pays more, searches less or loses trust.
reading_paths.limit: The current sources do not follow the same household from price display to final budget and repeat behavior.

edges.limit: The energy and credit sources do not identify the same household or the later repayment outcome.

edges.relation: Travel cost and time can change which work a household can keep

edges.relation: The value of a place depends on its wages, housing cost and route to opportunity

edges.relation: Vehicle, fuel and insurance costs can take room from other household payments

edges.relation: A payment system needs a usable answer when a customer reports a loss

edges.relation: A short credit bridge and an education loan can both turn today's choice into a later payment claim

edges.relation: Payment trouble may reduce room for a housing choice

edges.relation: Repayment rules can meet career and public-service choices

edges.relation: Unpaid eldercare can use hours that are also needed for paid work

edges.relation: Familiar speech may shape access to people-facing work and advancement
edges.limit: The current HBS evidence shows job sorting, not a direct hiring, promotion or pay decision for a specific worker.

edges.relation: A career-level measure can show movement that titles and years alone hide
edges.limit: The measure does not show whether slower movement was chosen or imposed, or whether work became less secure.

edges.relation: Slower career movement may leave less room for a long education-debt payment
edges.limit: No current source follows career progression and student-loan payment for the same borrower.

edges.relation: A clearly explained ownership claim may change whether workers stay and how they see daily work
edges.limit: The current study measures retention and identification, not effort, safety, customer outcomes or decision power.

edges.relation: Work conditions and rewards determine whether a financial claim becomes household room
edges.limit: The current work and ownership sources do not follow the same worker from job conditions to pay, savings or wealth.

edges.relation: Planned in-person contact may change communication, feedback and retention in remote work
edges.limit: The current trial concerns one employer and does not show effects on pay, promotion or worker choice.

edges.relation: A social cost can change whether people use a tool meant to protect their attention
edges.limit: The current study uses stated choices and trust tasks; it does not connect aid choice to later attention use in the same US consumers.

edges.relation: A payment that continues after value fades can reduce room in the household budget
edges.limit: The current study estimates seller revenue under different attention assumptions; it does not measure the customer's later budget or hardship.

edges.relation: The form and timing of public help may change how a household uses the program
edges.limit: The current evidence measures spending response, not whether one design improves access, security or later trust more than another.

edges.relation: Repeated prices and wage comparisons can change the room a household thinks it has
edges.limit: The current survey and retail evidence do not measure the same household's actual budget or purchase change.

edges.relation: A delayed trade-policy cost can become part of the price people use to judge the economy

edges.relation: The number of jobs can change what work gives a household beyond its pay
edges.limit: The current evidence shows spending differences but does not isolate the role of job structure from worker and household selection.

edges.relation: A depositor's staying habit may leave less interest in the household budget while giving the bank steadier funding

edges.relation: Privacy protection may change whether a person feels safe enough to use and share through a service
edges.limit: The current evidence shows more sharing on one platform but does not measure service quality, later use or customer power.

edges.relation: Local real-wage loss may shape which prices people use to judge the economy and the party in power
edges.limit: The current county study does not identify each voter's price basket, wage change, blame or reason for voting.

edges.relation: A weaker local tie among business owners may change who controls local services and opportunity
edges.limit: The current evidence does not show that owner movement changed local jobs, prices, services or belonging.

edges.relation: A rate message may change how households read future prices and their own buying power
edges.limit: The current evidence does not identify which households change beliefs and later purchases or savings in their records.

edges.relation: Health and independence can change both what older customers need and what care costs them
edges.limit: The current marketing and aging studies do not measure the same customer's product access, care use, price or well-being.

edges.relation: Emotional support can change both how long a person stays and whether leaving feels possible
edges.limit: The current evidence does not show whether longer use reflects benefit, dependence or a failure to reach human care.

edges.relation: A repair can turn a normal route to work or care into a cash and access problem
edges.limit: The current sources do not show which households lose a trip or whether another route was available.

edges.relation: A family may cover a shock with money or unpaid care before a formal service arrives

edges.relation: A household cash choice can change what a small business can keep investing in or offering

edges.limit: The current evidence does not show the same family's total resources after benefit loss and added pay.

edges.relation: The job can carry health coverage that changes the cost of leaving

edges.relation: Medical debt relief can change a credit path even when the health problem remains

edges.relation: Regular cash can change whether a household can stay, move or live more independently

edges.relation: A benefit change can become part of how households judge the policy and the economy

edges.relation: A less predictable paycheck can change what work leaves a household able to plan and buy

edges.limit: The current evidence does not show whether the financed purchase protected access or reduced later financial room.
